claims.claim: A brand is the audience's overall perception of an organization, product, or service: an intangible asset made up of the organization's own efforts plus the meaning customers attach to it. The American Marketing Association defines a brand as a distinctive feature such as a name, term, design, or symbol that identifies and distinguishes one seller's goods or services from others.

Branding is the ongoing process of developing and shaping a brand; every product, promotion, and event either reinforces or erodes the brand, so branding is an activity carried on over time rather than a one-time act.

Brand identity is the designed, tangible system through which a brand is expressed and recognized: brand name, logo/brand mark, color, typography, imagery, and verbal voice, protected in part by trademark.
Brand equity is the additional value a brand has over a substitute product; when consumers will pay more for a branded item than for a near-identical alternative, that difference is brand equity.

Brand positioning can be built on product attributes, on customer benefits, or on shared values; values-based positioning that connects to consumers' personal beliefs is presented as the most robust of the three.

Consistency across every touchpoint is what builds a brand's value over time: each product, promotion, and event must reinforce the same brand so recognition and emotional connection accumulate rather than fragment.
A brand's visual identity gives an organization a consistent look across a logo, colors, and typography, and building and maintaining that identity system is part of the graphic designer's work.
A logo is one element of a brand identity system, not the whole brand; the mark signals the identity but the brand itself is the broader perception it triggers.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Popular sources use 'brand', 'branding', and 'brand identity' loosely and sometimes interchangeably.
positions: Trade blogs often equate 'brand' with 'logo' or with the visual identity.
Marketing texts (OpenStax) separate brand (perception/feeling and value) from branding (the process of developing it), with identity elements as the tangible expression.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Followed the OpenStax/AMA distinction: brand = perception held by the audience, brand identity = the designed system that expresses it, branding = the ongoing activity of shaping perception. Flagged the logo=brand conflation as a common mistake.
